newsitem.title: UK: Meningitis scare hits British university.
newsitem.headline: Meningitis scare hits British university.

text.p: Students at a British university were ordered on Saturday to avoid kissing and all other forms of initimate contact after a deadly meningitis outbreak.

Health officials, who are busy probing how the cluster of cases developed on the campus at Cardiff, 140 miles (225 km) west of London, said the outbreak was extremely rare and warranted a speedy and serious reaction.
"Everyone is behaving very responsibly. I have certainly not seen any panic among the students," said Dr Bill Smith, chief medical officer for Bro Taf Health Authority.
Vaccinations were planned for 770 students at the University of Wales. Antibiotics have already been administered following the death of a 19-year-old woman hours after she was taken ill.
A law student from London, the woman fell ill while attending a lecture on Thursday. She died the same night.
Four other people have so far been affected.
A 20-year-old man is described as "stable" in intensive care. Another two people are said to be "doing well".
A student admitted to hospital late on Friday night has now also developed signs of the life-threatening disease.
"It has been quite a morbid atmosphere," said one student.
With bars closed and parties cancelled on medical advice, students were advised to avoid close physical contact.
Many were reported to have left the campus in fright.

The meningistis struck as Britain grappled with its worst outbreak of food poisoning for a decade. Suspect meat in Scotland has been blamed for the death of at least five people. Hundreds more have fallen ill.
